free_text: The patient is a 68-year-old male with a rising PSA of 11.7 ng/mL and a cT1c prostate cancer, with a PI-RADS 4 lesion identified on MRI. Histologically, the Gleason score is 3+3 (ISUP Grade Group 1), with recent biopsy showing perineural invasion. The management assessment is active surveillance, balancing potential treatment benefit against patient preferences.
